subject: SLO & rate-limit sync: parallel requests, connection pool, and next steps
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Tan <alice.tan@finpay.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: latency/throughput targets + next steps

Hi Alice — great call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the tech sync:

- FinPay targets we captured: 95th latency target for API responses <= 120ms for single-turn requests; streaming support for partial results on larger payloads; average steady-state throughput ~250 rps, peak bursts up to 600 rps during settlement windows.
- Concurrency: FinPay expects up to 80 parallel requests from a single integration during peaks (clients will multiplex several users).
- Our defaults: Redwood hosted rate limits are typically 100 rps per API key and 50 concurrent connections; we can propose either a temporary quota bump for PoC or a Dedicated pool for production.

Attachments: I attached a lightweight load-test plan (finpay-loadtest-plan.xlsx) that outlines the scenarios we discussed.

Next suggested steps: 
1) You confirm the peak/steady numbers above.
2) We do a short tech sync with your DevOps (30-45m) to walk connection-pool and streaming behavior.
3) Redwood to propose two options by Thu: (A) hosted + quota increase for PoC (temporary bump + canary), (B) Dedicated capacity quote and autoscale profile.

If that works I’ll loop in Solutions and Engs to draft the temporary SLA exception and cost delta.

Thanks,
Rafael
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai

From: Alice Tan <alice.tan@finpay.io>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Victor Gomez <victor.gomez@finpay.io>, DevOps Team <devops@finpay.io>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: latency/throughput targets + next steps

Rafael — thanks for the recap and the load-test plan. Mostly aligned, a few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: 95th <= 150ms is acceptable for the first phase if it helps reduce cost; long-term goal is 120ms.
- Streaming: yes — we need server-sent events / chunked responses for long-running responses (UX depends on partial tokens delivered within 200ms of first token).
- Throughput: steady ~250 rps, but our clearing window can spike up to 1,000 rps for ~30s; that’s the hard-case we need to validate.
- Concurrency: our integration will open up to 80 parallel long-lived streams per region (US-east primarily).

We also have some security/network constraints: egress from our VPC goes through a NAT with limited ephemeral ports; happy to share network topology if that influences connection pooling guidance.

I’ve attached the quick infra notes from our DevOps team. Can you and your engineering folks confirm whether the temporary quota bump you mentioned can handle 1,000 rps bursts and 80 concurrent streaming connections, or if we need a Dedicated pool for the PoC?

Thanks — Alice
Product Owner, FinPay

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: FinPay PoC — ask to Ops/Platform for options

Quick internal note following Alice’s reply: 

Summary of ask: FinPay needs to validate steady ~250 rps, and short bursts up to 1,000 rps (30s), with up to 80 concurrent long-lived streaming connections. They prefer hosted but will consider Dedicated if quota bump is insufficient.

Questions for Eng/Platform (Karthik):
- Can hosted rate limits be temporarily bumped to 1,000 rps with 150 concurrent connections for a two-week PoC? What are the failure modes (throttling headers, backpressure, token-bucket behaviour)?
- Streaming: confirm whether Redwood streaming path supports interleaved partial tokens at sub-200ms first-token latency for long-lived streams at scale.
- Connection pooling: best practices (keep-alive, max sockets per host) for customers behind NATs. FinPay may hit ephemeral port limits.

Action: Karthik, can you propose (A) a hosted-temporary-bump plan with monitoring/rollback and (B) a Dedicated pool quote including estimated cost delta? I’ll draft the SLA exception and attach to the PoC doc.

Thanks — Rafael
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 14:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Internal: FinPay PoC — ask to Ops/Platform for options

Rafael / team — based on the ask here are two pragmatic options and what we need from FinPay to proceed:

Option A — Hosted + temporary quota bump (fastest path):
- Proposed PoC quota: 1,000 rps burst capacity with soft-steady 300 rps; concurrency limit raised to 150 concurrent connections for the FinPay API key(s).
- Safety controls: rate-limited ramp (token-bucket, 3x ramp over 10 minutes), per-token accounting visible in Console, automated rollback if error-rate or latency regressions exceed thresholds.
- Cost: incremental usage billing + a temporary surcharge for the quota exception.
- Engineering impact: small — mostly config + monitoring. We’ll add request headers X-Redwood-Rate-Limit and advisory guidance.

Option B — Dedicated pool (recommended for production):
- Dedicated GPU pool with reserved capacity sized for sustained 500 rps (per-region) and burst headroom to 2,000 rps across autoscaling windows; concurrent streaming optimized by keeping larger KV caches and sticky routing.
- Connection-pool guidance: recommend keep-alive and HTTP/2 multiplexing where possible; max simultaneous sockets per client should be tuned (we recommend up to 100 sockets for FinPay given NAT port limits) and use multiple API keys to shard bursts if needed.
- Cost: higher fixed monthly commit, predictable SLAs.

For streaming-specific behavior: the runtime supports chunked streaming with low first-token latency in our dedicated paths; on hosted we can meet ~200ms first-token in most cases but will validate in the PoC load test (network variance included).

Requested from FinPay before we proceed:
1) Confirm whether they can run the ramp profile in the attached load-test plan (I’ll add the exact script).
2) Confirm ephemeral port constraints / NAT topology.
3) If they accept Option A for PoC, legal needs a short SLA exception doc (I prepared a draft — see sla-exception-request.pdf).

I’ll drop a quick cost delta for Option A vs B by EOD tomorrow.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Tan <alice.tan@finpay.io>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: FinPay mutual action plan & proposed schedule

Hi Alice — looping in the proposed mutual action plan so everyone has clarity: 

1) PoC setup (week of Nov 29): Redwood config Option A (hosted + quota bump) staged for FinPay test key; short smoke tests on Nov 29; full load test Nov 30.
2) Load test validation: run the scenarios in finpay-loadtest-plan.xlsx; Redwood to provide real-time dashboards + token/latency traces.
3) Decision point: if Option A meets the burst/concurrency targets with acceptable latency, move to a 30-day pilot. If not, we’ll fast-track Dedicated sizing and a production commit.
4) Procurement & legal: Rafael will send SLA exception and PO/DocuSign. FinPay to return signed PO to begin billing for PoC surcharge.

I’ve created a DocuSign envelope for the PO and attached the draft SLA exception (sla-exception-request.pdf). Rafael — can you confirm the Nov 29 smoke test time (30–45m) and invite the FinPay DevOps owners?

Thanks,
Monica
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Monica / Rafael — confirmed. FinPay accepts Option A for the PoC (hosted + temporary quota bump) and we will run the smoke test on Nov 29 at 10:00 AM ET.

We completed an internal review and are provisionally okay with the SLA exception for the PoC; I attached the signed PO stub and the contact for our DevOps lead (devops@finpay.io). Please include rate-limit headers in responses and send recommended connection-pooling snippets (we prefer examples for HTTP/2 + keep-alive).

Victor will be on the Nov 29 call for a quick sign-off. Thanks for moving quickly.

—Alice
Product Owner, FinPay
